make.sh writes a whole build.nbt: Shell B placed 1537 blocks with 0 refused writes, and the structure check finds no floating or unsupported blocks.
left: Roofs, porch decks and steps, shutters, windows and doors are not mine: plot 4 porch deck y2 and steps, plot 7 porch steps and railings, and the picnic table are unbuilt and left to fittings and grounds.

Barn: the stair part's ladder at (62,1..6,14) takes the stall B back cell, so the feed rack there is skipped and only three racks stand. The stall pens are hand-drawn to plan.md rather than mule_stall(), whose partition runs on the other axis.

water_tank writes water in the tank, which is off-palette (x8 in parts-report). The plan names it, so I kept the helper's output.
Plot 6 oven: the stack and fire at (75,2,16) belong to the chimney part; fit flags an open flue there that the chimney part should close.

elements.md ticked only for the barn stalls, hay loft and loft ladder, the water tank, and the duplex party wall, belt and cornice. The other plot 4/5/6/7 items wait on roofs, fittings or chimneys; plan.md has no checklist to tick.

waste.what: Hand-computed every wall line, opening and lintel coordinate from the FACADES and OPENINGS tables, one line per box
waste.cost: about 15 wall calls and 25 opening boxes of coordinate work
waste.tool: A helper that takes a plot's OPENINGS rows and the wall line, and emits clapboard_wall or a stone-course wall with lintels, would make this a few lines.

waste.what: Wrote the barn stall pens by hand because mule_stall() puts its partition on the other axis from plan.md
waste.cost: about 12 set() calls and one retry after a fence/gate orientation mistake
waste.tool: mule_stall with an axis option (partition along z at the row) matching plan.md's stall layout.

waste.what: Worked out which cells the stair flights carve (floor holes, ladder cells) so my writes would not be refused
waste.cost: one make.sh pass to confirm 0 refused, plus reading stairs.mjs by hand
waste.tool: runParts printing the reserved cells of earlier parts (holes, ladder cells) before a part runs, so shell parts can skip them.

waste.what: Checked the piers, ground floors and walls by eye from the sheet and the elevations
waste.cost: one render and one read of the sheet
waste.tool: A per-plot render crop at standing eye height, so a shell's windows and gables can be checked without roof and fittings.

companions.task: Plinth courses, the bread-oven vault and its lintels, and the duplex's stone-brick lintels and belt, so the masonry reads as dressed work rather than plain fill.
The barn's board-and-batten gables, the gambrel loft floor and hay drop, and the stall pens with their gate hinges.
Confirm that the stair holes in the plot 4 attic and the duplex upper floors line up with the flights, and that the duplex landing stands on a solid floor.
